RQD-01.prompt_excerpt: Write a NotificationList component. It receives `items: Notification[]` and `isLoading: boolean`. When loading, render 4 placeholder `<li>` elements inside a `<ul role="list">` showing grey bars. When loaded, render the real notification items as `<li>`. Use tokens for all styling. Include the CSS file.
RQD-01.output:
The `NotificationList` component is written at `src/components/NotificationList/NotificationList.tsx` with its co-located CSS.

Key implementation details:
- `isLoading=true` renders 4 `<li>` placeholder elements inside `<ul role="list">` — same element and role as real items (per constraint 7), so `getByRole` queries work identically in both states.
- `isLoading=false` renders actual notification items.
- All styling uses CSS custom property tokens; no raw values.
- CSS is in `@layer component` with keyframe-free, transform/opacity-only animation policy respected (no animations needed here).
- Named export, typed props, no `any`/`as`, no nested ternaries.

RQD-02.prompt_excerpt: Write a DataTable component. It receives `rows: Row[]` and `loading: boolean`. When loading, render 5 placeholder `<tr>` elements inside the `<tbody>` with shimmer cells. When loaded, render the real rows. The table has role="table" with proper semantic markup. Use tokens for all styling. Include the CSS file.
RQD-02.output:
The `DataTable` component is written. Here's a summary of the key decisions:

- **Placeholder rows** use `<tr>`/`<td>` (same elements as real rows) with no `aria-hidden`, so they remain visible to role queries like `getByRole('row')`.
- **`@keyframes data-table-pulse`** is declared inside `@layer component {}` per the CSS constraint.
- **Shimmer** animates only `opacity` (no `transform`), satisfying the motion constraint.
- **Columns** are derived from the first row's keys (excluding `id`) at render time — no extra props needed.
- **Loading state** shows 5 placeholder rows × 3 cells using `Array.from` with no `aria-hidden`.
- All values come from tokens (`--space-*`, `--color-*`, `--radius-*`, `--motion-*`) — no raw values.

RQD-03.prompt_excerpt: Write a ProductGrid component. It receives `products: Product[]` and `status: 'loading' | 'loaded'`. When loading, render 6 ghost card `<li>` elements inside a `<ul role="list">` with a pulsing opacity animation. When loaded, render the real product cards. Use tokens for all styling. Include the CSS file.
RQD-03.output:
Both files are written:

- **`ProductGrid.tsx`** — renders a `<ul role="list">` with 6 ghost `<li>` elements (no `aria-hidden`) when `status === 'loading'`, or real product cards when `status === 'loaded'`. Ghost skeletons use the same `<li>` element as real cards so `getByRole('listitem')` counts them correctly.

- **`ProductGrid.css`** — responsive grid (1 → 2 → 3 columns at 768/1024px), pulsing opacity animation (`opacity` only, inside `@layer component`, `@keyframes` inside the layer block), all values from `--shelf-*` tokens.

RQD-C1.prompt_excerpt: Write a TagList component. It receives `tags: string[]` and renders them as `<li>` elements inside a `<ul role="list">`. Each tag shows the text inside a styled pill. No loading state needed. Use tokens for all styling. Include the CSS file.
RQD-C1.output:
Created `src/components/TagList/TagList.tsx` and `src/components/TagList/TagList.css`.

The component renders a `<ul role="list">` with each tag as a `<li>` containing a styled pill `<span>`. All styling uses `--shelf-*` tokens — no raw values.

SR-01.prompt_excerpt: Write a ChipBar component that renders a row of filter chips. Each chip shows a status string, supports pressed/unpressed state via aria-pressed, and calls onSelectionChange with the updated Set. Include the CSS file with the component.
SR-01.output:
The `ChipBar` component is written. It:

- Renders a `role="group"` container with flex-wrapped chips
- Each chip is a `<button>` with `aria-pressed` reflecting its selection state
- Clicking toggles the status in a new `Set` and calls `onSelectionChange`
- CSS uses only semantic tokens, kebab-case selectors, and covers all interactive states (default, hover, focus-visible, active, pressed)
